glance: Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive agent app that works in the background and asks before it acts. At GTC Berlin, Nvidia made its cuDSS sparse solver generally available, with 8–10x speedups reported in Abaqus, and pushed its Halos and Hyperion stack for virtual validation of automated driving with Mercedes, Volvo and Porsche. On the money side, a leaked draft prospectus shows Anthropic at $16.3B in first-half revenue and $80.7B in net loss, and Meta raised its AI capex floor again.
brief: At GTC Berlin, Nvidia made its cuDSS sparse solver generally available, with eight to ten times speedups reported in Abaqus and support in STAR-CCM+ and COMSOL. The sparse solve is often the bottleneck in implicit finite-element and multiphysics runs, so this directly affects how many bearing and structural variants can be run in a day. Nvidia also pushed its Halos stack for simulation-led validation of automated driving, linking simulation, hardware-in-the-loop and fleet data, with Porsche targeting ninety percent fewer test drives. Mercedes, Audi and Schaeffler showed simulation-first workflows, from aerodynamic CFD to production and actuator twins, as Nvidia's factory agents went to early access. Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive agent that keeps working in the background and asks before it acts, a reference design built around an inbox of updates, a task list and approval gates rather than a chat box. A leaked draft prospectus gave the first hard look at frontier-lab economics: Anthropic made 16.3 billion dollars in revenue in the first half and booked an 80.7 billion dollar net loss. Meta beat on revenue but raised its AI spending floor again, pushing free cash flow negative. ChatGPT ads expanded to 89 countries with more than a hundred thousand advertisers. Perplexity's computer agent can now run fully on Apple silicon Macs, keeping files local. OpenAI bought Orchestra Bio to add drug-development agents, and Mistral shipped Voxtral 3, a European-hosted voice-agent stack that is relevant for in-car and data-sensitive products.
note: All summaries are paraphrased. Benchmark and speedup figures are vendor-reported. Anthropic's financials come from a draft prospectus reported by the WSJ and not confirmed by the company.

body: At GTC Berlin, Nvidia made cuDSS, its CUDA-X library for direct sparse linear solves, generally available. It moves the factorise-and-solve step of large sparse systems onto GPUs, scales from a workstation to a cluster, and can be called from C, C++, Python and Fortran.

Vendor numbers: Dassault Systèmes reports 8–10x faster structural and electromagnetic solves in Abaqus. Applied Materials reports up to 10x over CPU-only. ZEISS SMT, using COMSOL, reports 4x on an EUV plasma benchmark. Siemens is using it in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ for fluid-structure interaction, Synopsys in Sentaurus, and Cadence in Celsius for thermal stress and warpage. In the keynote, Dassault and Volkswagen also showed a design agent adapting a Golf door for the Tiguan, where a SIMULIA-based simulation agent flagged a vibration problem before the design was refined.

For OEM virtual validation, the practical question is whether your solver versions and licences expose the GPU path, and how much of your run time actually sits in the linear solve rather than contact iterations or I/O. If a test run shows a real speedup, you could move from a handful of design points to a proper DoE within the same time window.
stories.headline: Nvidia's cuDSS goes GA, bringing GPU sparse solvers to Abaqus, STAR-CCM+ and COMSOL
stories.why: The sparse linear solve is often the bottleneck in implicit FE and multiphysics runs, so this directly affects how many bearing and structural variants you can run per day.

body: Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a standalone app (iOS, Android and web) where Claude comes to you with what needs attention, completes tasks you assign, and keeps going on its own cloud computer after you close the app. It runs on Opus 5.5 and uses the same memory, skills and connectors as regular Claude. It is rolling out in waves to US Pro and Max subscribers from a waitlist, with Team and Enterprise to follow. There is no extra charge, but background work counts against plan limits.

The interaction model is worth studying. There is one main thread plus topic channels with shared memory, a daily brief built from mail and calendar, an Updates feed that flags decisions, a Tasks tab, and a Make tab holding finished deliverables as editable files. Duet asks before sending messages, paying, signing or deleting, and only the user can mark a task done.

This puts Anthropic up against OpenAI's Dots and Meta's Muse in the always-on assistant space. For product teams, it shows the patterns converging: proactive surfacing, explicit permission checkpoints, and outputs treated as artifacts rather than chat replies.
stories.headline: Anthropic previews Claude Duet, a proactive agent that keeps working when you leave
stories.why: A clear reference design for proactive, background agents: an inbox of updates, a task list and approval gates instead of a chat box.

body: The Wall Street Journal has seen a draft IPO prospectus. Anthropic has not confirmed it. The draft shows $16.3B in revenue for the first half of 2026, up from $1.1B a year earlier. Compute spending was nearly $9B, more than the whole of 2025. The $80.7B net loss is mostly a non-cash charge of about $72B tied to convertible notes and other financing instruments.

The filing reportedly lists roughly $450B in cloud agreements over a decade ($111B Google, $110B AWS, $31B Microsoft), more than $600B in total infrastructure commitments, and possibly up to $750B including deals still being negotiated. Two customers made up about 20% of revenue. Investor talk has moved from about $2T toward about $1.5T, and Bloomberg reports a target of listing before Thanksgiving.

For product teams, the takeaway is that model pricing and capacity are tied to very large fixed commitments. Expect continued pushes on usage-based plans, enterprise lock-in and price tiers, and treat any single-vendor dependency as a risk to manage.
stories.headline: Draft prospectus: Anthropic made $16.3B in revenue in H1 and booked an $80.7B net loss
stories.why: The first hard look at frontier-lab economics. Compute commitments and customer concentration will shape pricing and API stability for everyone building on these models.

body: Nvidia launched Halos SAFE, a safety assurance framework that connects simulation, hardware- and software-in-the-loop, on-road testing and fleet monitoring into one evidence chain. dSPACE, IVEX and TÜV Rheinland are collaborating on it, and JLR, Mercedes-Benz, Volvo Cars, AVL, Foretellix and Synopsys are part of the ecosystem. New Cosmos 3 Nano variants generate synchronised multi-camera and lidar data for closed-loop simulation.

On the OEM side, Mercedes-Benz extends its partnership for L3 and L4 work. Volvo Cars adopts Hyperion and the Alpamayo stack. VW Commercial Vehicles shows its ID. Buzz AD. Bolt plans a European robotaxi programme on at least 25,000 future Lucid vehicles, starting data collection in Madrid in 2027. Porsche says its data flywheel for VW Group could cut repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and development cycles by up to 85%. Both figures are expectations, not results.

For virtual validation teams, the signal is that toolchain vendors and certifiers are lining up around simulation evidence that counts toward homologation. The open question is how regulators will weigh synthetic data against physical miles.
stories.headline: Nvidia's Halos SAFE links simulation, XiL and fleet data for AV validation, and Porsche targets 90% fewer test drives

links.label: GlobeNewswire – European mobility leaders on Hyperion

stories.why: A concrete vendor framework for simulation-led sign-off, with familiar validation names: dSPACE, AVL, TÜV Rheinland.

body: Nvidia released its Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX) in early access on GitHub. It is a template for an always-on factory manager agent plus specialist agents for inspection, root-cause analysis and reporting, connecting to CAD, PLM, simulation and IT/OT systems. Siemens estimates about 20% cost savings from FOX-based root-cause agents and a 40% cut in inspection calibration time at Erlangen.

Several automotive examples were shown. Mercedes-Benz runs STAR-CCM+ on GPUs for faster aerodynamic simulation and uses vision agents to verify windshield assembly. Audi tests battery-production concepts in an Omniverse twin before the equipment exists. Schaeffler is integrating digital twins of humanoid-robot actuators with Isaac simulation to reduce physical testing. Dassault's Nemotron-based virtual companions work with CATIA and SIMULIA agents to design and virtually test vehicle doors, and Autodesk brings simulation-trained surrogate models into Alias.
Schaeffler's actuator-twin work is closest to bearing and drivetrain component validation. It's worth watching whether it extends to bearing-level models.
stories.headline: Factory agents go to early access, as Mercedes, Audi and Schaeffler show simulation-first workflows
stories.why: Shows where European OEMs and suppliers are using AI in engineering right now: aero CFD, production twins and actuator twins.

body: Meta reported Q3 revenue of $64.6B, up 26% year on year and above consensus. Net income fell to $9.9B, hit by a $10B youth-safety settlement charge. Q3 capex was $34.9B, and full-year guidance moved to $135–145B, raising the low end by $5B. Free cash flow was negative $2.1B, against $10.6B a year earlier.

Meta also announced a non-voting Class C share, issued as a stock dividend and taking effect 19 January 2027. It effectively works like a two-for-one split and gives Meta a currency for funding and compensation without diluting control. Reality Labs is expected to lose about $15B in 2027 as investment shifts to AI. 2027 capex has not been guided yet, but Meta says it will keep investing aggressively.

For strategy work, the picture is that the largest consumer platforms are betting their margins on AI assistants. Expect aggressive bundling of Muse into Meta's apps and more pressure on smaller assistant products to differentiate on trust or niche depth.
stories.headline: Meta beats on revenue but raises its AI capex floor, and free cash flow turns negative

links.label: StockTitan – Meta Q3 and Class C

stories.why: Ad revenue is paying for AI infrastructure at a scale that pushes even Meta into negative free cash flow, and it shapes how Meta prices and ships Muse.

body: OpenAI added 26 markets to ChatGPT Ads, including 14 more in Latin America plus Nigeria, South Africa, Serbia, Ukraine, Pakistan and Bangladesh, for 89 countries in total. Ads appear only on the Free and Go tiers. They are labelled and kept separate from answers, and withheld from under-18s and from sensitive topics such as health and politics. OpenAI says more than 100,000 advertisers have signed up in about eight months, with buying through partners or a self-serve Ads Manager.
OpenAI says the next phase brings new formats, objectives and measurement. European markets were added earlier in the pilot.

For PMs and growth teams, this makes 'answer-engine' visibility a paid and organic channel in its own right. It also sets a precedent for freemium AI products: ads on the cheap tier, a clean experience on paid tiers.
stories.headline: ChatGPT ads expand to 89 countries, with more than 100,000 advertisers in eight months
stories.why: Conversational ads are becoming a real channel, and a new surface where your product could be recommended, or advertised against.

body: Perplexity added a local-first mode to its Mac app. Both the model and the agent that directs tasks run on the device, even offline. Users download local models (Qwen 3.6 and Perplexity's own PPLX Pro), and Perplexity recommends at least 36GB of unified memory. With permission, the agent can work with local files and apps such as Notes, Mail, Messages and Numbers.

Cloud access becomes an explicit opt-in per task, for fresh web information, browser use or connected apps, and the existing Hybrid Compute mode is still available in the same app. It is included for Pro, Max and Enterprise subscribers.

For designers, this is a useful pattern to note: a visible boundary between local and cloud work, with escalation only when the user approves. It could matter for European and regulated users, where data residency is often the main objection to agent tools.
stories.headline: Perplexity's Computer agent can now run fully on-device on Apple silicon Macs
stories.why: Local-first agents change the privacy and permission UX: files stay on the machine unless the user explicitly approves cloud access.

body: OpenAI acquired Orchestra Bio, a startup whose agents help pharma teams coordinate drug development. They track clinical trials, flag knock-on effects on timelines when something fails (such as a production batch), and suggest next steps. Terms were not disclosed.

Orchestra will be folded into Rosalind, OpenAI's life-sciences platform built around the GPT-Rosalind reasoning model and the Rosalind Workbench. The goal is agents that connect lab findings to trial operations and decisions. OpenAI already works with Novo Nordisk and Moderna.

The pattern matters beyond pharma: frontier labs are buying domain workflow tools to sit closer to where decisions happen, not just selling model access. A similar move into PLM, test management or CAE workflows would directly affect vehicle development tooling.
stories.headline: OpenAI buys Orchestra Bio to add drug-development workflow agents to Rosalind
stories.why: Labs are moving from general models toward vertical, workflow-owning products. Expect the same playbook in engineering and manufacturing.

body: Mistral released Voxtral 3. It includes Voxtral Small Transcribe 3 for speech-to-text in more than 50 languages, and Voxtral Mini TTS 3 for text-to-speech in over 35 languages and 50 dialects, with emotional adaptation. Transcription starts at $0.0035 per minute.

A voice-agent SDK built on LiveKit handles listening, reasoning, tool calls and speech in a single streaming pipeline, so an agent can, for example, look up an invoice or book an appointment mid-call. It is available through Mistral's EU-hosted API or on the customer's own infrastructure. Licensing and latency figures were not detailed in coverage.

The same day, ElevenLabs launched Eleven Realtime speech-to-speech models. Voice is quickly becoming a commodity layer, so differentiation moves to turn-taking, error recovery and handing off to visual UI.
stories.headline: Mistral ships Voxtral 3, an EU-hosted voice-agent stack with transcription from $0.0035 a minute
stories.why: A European option for voice interfaces that can run on your own infrastructure, which matters for in-car and data-sensitive products.
